claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its high-entropy-alloy derivatives have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
Introducing a secondary phase with high magnetic anisotropy can increase the coercive field of alloys derived from single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Composition modification or processing can introduce the proposed secondary phase.
The secondary phase should be uniformly distributed.
The secondary-phase size should be smaller than the magnetic domain size.
The secondary phase acts as a pinning site for magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning by the secondary phase increases the energy required for domain-wall motion.
Introducing the high-anisotropy secondary phase increases the magnetic anisotropy of the material.
Increased magnetic anisotropy leads to increased coercive field.
The intervention will produce a coercive-field increase greater than 100 Oe relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a derivative.
Keeping the secondary-phase volume fraction at or below 20% avoids a significant reduction in saturation magnetization.
Samples spanning secondary-phase volume fractions from 5% to 20% should be prepared and compared with the baseline.
Coercive field and saturation magnetization will be measured, together with microstructural characterization.
The hypothesis is falsified if no sample containing 5% to 20% secondary phase shows at least a 20% coercive-field increase over the baseline.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies an absolute coercive-field increase greater than 100 Oe, whereas the falsification rule tests only whether a relative increase of at least 20% occurs. A sample could satisfy the 20% rule while falling far short of the stated prediction.
